name: Scopolamine
metabolism: How the body breaks it down has not yet been verified for this entry. No enzymes, breakdown products or elimination routes are specified.
summary: Scopolamine, also known as hyoscine, is a muscarinic antagonist used for motion sickness and postoperative nausea and vomiting. It is available in oral, injectable, and transdermal forms.
toxicities: Common label-reported effects include dry mouth, drowsiness, blurred vision, dizziness, pupil dilation, agitation, and confusion.

Serious risks include acute angle-closure glaucoma, seizures, psychiatric/cognitive reactions, urinary retention, reduced gastrointestinal motility, and potentially fatal hyperthermia. Withdrawal symptoms may begin 24 hours or more after patch removal following several days of use.
Overdose can cause severe anticholinergic toxicity, including agitation, confusion, hallucinations, seizures, coma, hyperthermia, tachyarrhythmias, urinary retention, and visual disturbance.
generalRisks: The label for the transdermal system contraindicates use in angle-closure glaucoma and warns of cognitive and psychiatric effects, seizures, impaired driving, urinary retention, reduced gastrointestinal motility, and potentially fatal hyperthermia, especially with heat exposure. Withdrawal symptoms can occur a day or more after removal following several days of use. Overdose can cause severe central and peripheral anticholinergic toxicity.
saferUse: Use only the labeled transdermal system: wear one at a time and do not cut it. Wash hands after applying or removing it and prevent accidental contact or ingestion.
Avoid driving and hazardous activities until effects are known; alcohol, sedatives, opioids, and other anticholinergic drugs may intensify cognitive and CNS effects.

Remove the system and seek medical advice for overheating, reduced sweating, acute eye pain/halos, confusion, seizure, or difficulty urinating. After several days of use, watch for withdrawal symptoms after removal.
dosageRemark: The label is for prescription transdermal prevention of motion sickness or postoperative nausea. The labeled system delivers 1 mg over 3 days; this therapeutic specification is not recreational dose guidance, and no recreational thresholds are established here.
